newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares hold onto gains made on new premier.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares hold onto gains made on new premier.

text.p: ** (0815 GMT) - Bombay shares drift in positive territory
in afternoon trade, focus on safe passage of budget,
parliament will debate budget after April 30-official
** Bombay's benchmark share index up 66.17 points, or
** Parliament will not take up 1997/98 (April-March) budget
proposal until after April 30 - government official
** Inder Kumar Gujral is sworn in as Prime Minister,
decides to take finance minister portfolio, speculation
Chidambaram may be wooed back to re-take Finance
** Gujral is due to face a trust vote Tuesday at 0530 GMT

Bombay shares in mid-afternoon trading on Monday held onto gains made following the appointment of Inder Kumar Gujral as India's new prime minister and on growing confidence a pro-market 1997/98 (April-March) budget will be passed, dealers said.
"The market is looking for an immediate solution to the safe passage of the budget," a dealer at a foreign broking firm said.

The speaker of India's lower house, P.A. Sangma said the new prime minister wanted to push through parliament the budget proposed by former finance minister P.Chidambaram, whose party quit the government following Gujral's nomination.
